Y=(p​Re​O¯p​Im​O¯)∈ℝ2​Nw×P,e=(p​Re​εp​Im​ε),Y=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt{p}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\bar{O}\\ \sqrt{p}\,\mathrm{Im}\,\bar{O}\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{2N_{w}\times P},\qquad e=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt{p}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\varepsilon\\ \sqrt{p}\,\mathrm{Im}\,\varepsilon\end{pmatrix}, (S34)

gives S=YT​YS=Y^{T}Y with Sk​l=Re​∑sps​O¯s​k∗​O¯s​lS_{kl}=\mathrm{Re}\sum_{s}p_{s}\bar{O}^{*}_{sk}\bar{O}_{sl}, the quantum metric, and (YT​e)k=Re​∑sps​O¯s​k∗​εs=12​∂θkE¯(Y^{T}e)_{k}=\mathrm{Re}\sum_{s}p_{s}\bar{O}^{*}_{sk}\varepsilon_{s}=\frac{1}{2}\partial_{\theta_{k}}\bar{E}. The update direction solves

(S+λ​I)​δ=YT​e,λ=10−2​tr​S/P.(S+\lambda I)\,\delta=Y^{T}e,\qquad\lambda=10^{-2}\,\mathrm{tr}\,S/P. (S35)

Equivalently, δ\delta minimizes |Y​δ−e|2+λ​|δ|2|Y\delta-e|^{2}+\lambda|\delta|^{2}. Changing the parameters by −δ-\delta changes log⁡Ψ\log\Psi by −O¯​δ≈−ε-\bar{O}\delta\approx-\varepsilon, giving the best tangent-space approximation to a short step of imaginary-time evolution e−τ​H\mathrm{e}^{-\tau H}. For all reported optimizations, we solve Eq. (S35) by preconditioned conjugate gradients. We apply SS as S​v=YT​(Y​v)Sv=Y^{T}(Yv) and use the diagonal preconditioner (diag​S+λ)−1(\mathrm{diag}\,S+\lambda)^{-1}. The solver uses at most 60 iterations and a relative tolerance of 10−610^{-6}, after which we update the parameters according to

θ←θ−ηt​st​δ,ηt=0.021+t/2000,st=min⁡(1,0.05ηt​|Y​δ|).\theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta_{t}s_{t}\,\delta,\qquad\eta_{t}=\frac{0.02}{1+t/2000},\qquad s_{t}=\min\Big(1,\frac{0.05}{\eta_{t}|Y\delta|}\Big). (S36)

Since |Y​δ|2=δT​S​δ|Y\delta|^{2}=\delta^{T}S\delta, the quantity ηt​st​|Y​δ|\eta_{t}s_{t}|Y\delta| is the Fubini–Study length of the update to leading order, and the rescaling limits each change in the normalized state to 0.05. We skip updates with non-finite entries.

Cost and runs.

Each training iteration requires, per walker, 10 evaluations of Re​log⁡Ψ\mathrm{Re}\log\Psi, one forward-Laplacian pass and one reverse pass for OO, with the forward Laplacian accounting for most of the cost. Runs typically last 1000–3000 iterations, and larger systems are initialized from trained states at smaller sizes.

Evaluation.

After training, we hold the variational parameters and proposal scale σ\sigma fixed. A standard evaluation uses Nr=20N_{r}=20 rounds separated by 20 Metropolis steps. We first average the real local energy over rounds within each walker, then use the spread of these independent walker means to estimate the standard error,

E=1Nr​Nw​∑r,wRe​EL​(Xw(r)),σE=stdw​(E¯w)Nw,E¯w=1Nr​∑rRe​EL​(Xw(r)).E=\frac{1}{N_{r}N_{w}}\sum_{r,w}\mathrm{Re}\,E_{L}(X_{w}^{(r)}),\qquad\sigma_{E}=\frac{\mathrm{std}_{w}(\bar{E}_{w})}{\sqrt{N_{w}}},\qquad\bar{E}_{w}=\frac{1}{N_{r}}\sum_{r}\mathrm{Re}\,E_{L}(X_{w}^{(r)}). (S37)

If successive measurements within each walker are independent, the standard error is σL/Nw​Nr\sigma_{L}/\sqrt{N_{w}N_{r}}, where σL2=⟨(Re​EL)2⟩−E2\sigma_{L}^{2}=\langle(\mathrm{Re}\,E_{L})^{2}\rangle-E^{2} is the variance of one measurement. For correlated measurements and runs long compared with the correlation time, the effective sample count is Neff≃Nw​Nr/[1+2​∑t≥1ρE​(t)]N_{\rm eff}\simeq N_{w}N_{r}/[1+2\sum_{t\geq 1}\rho_{E}(t)], where ρE​(t)\rho_{E}(t) is the normalized autocorrelation of the real local energy at a lag of tt measurement rounds. The reported errors use stdw​(E¯w)\mathrm{std}_{w}(\bar{E}_{w}) directly, so the spread of walker means includes these correlations. The angular momentum 𝐋=∑i[𝐫i×(−i​∇i−𝐀i)+qb​g2​𝐧i]\mathbf{L}=\sum_{i}[\mathbf{r}_{i}\times(-\mathrm{i}\nabla_{i}-\mathbf{A}_{i})+\frac{q_{bg}}{2}\mathbf{n}_{i}] is Hermitian, so

⟨L2⟩=∑a=x,y,z⟨|La​ΨΨ|2⟩,𝐋​ΨΨ=∑i[−i𝐫i×∇ilogΨ−𝐫i×𝐀i+qb​g2𝐧i],\langle L^{2}\rangle=\sum_{a=x,y,z}\Big\langle\Big|\frac{L_{a}\Psi}{\Psi}\Big|^{2}\Big\rangle,\qquad\frac{\mathbf{L}\Psi}{\Psi}=\sum_{i}\Big[-\mathrm{i}\,\mathbf{r}_{i}\times\nabla_{i}\log\Psi-\mathbf{r}_{i}\times\mathbf{A}_{i}+\frac{q_{bg}}{2}\mathbf{n}_{i}\Big], (S38)

which needs first derivatives only. We classify a state as rotation invariant (uniform) when ⟨L2⟩≤3\langle L^{2}\rangle\leq 3. States with var/N>1.5\mathrm{var}/N>1.5 near the crystal are re-evaluated with 200 rounds of 1024 walkers after 100 thermalization rounds (“reeval” in the data). Running means at 20, 50, 100 and 200 rounds are stored to show convergence.

Extrapolation.

We extrapolate within each shift sector qb​gq_{bg} using linear fits E/N=e∞+b/NE/N=e_{\infty}+b/N, since the shift enters only at order 1/N1/N. For the disk, the boundary adds a term a/Na/\sqrt{N} (Sec. S5.1). We estimate fit uncertainties from the residual scatter, as optimization errors dominate the VMC uncertainties.

S3 Parameter-free analytical wavefunctions

Here we give the analytical wavefunctions of the color-superconductor ansatz. They arise from pairing of the holon metal, whose partons carry a color index with SU(NcN_{c}) gauge symmetry. We use the physical particle coordinates without backflow. With Nc=1/αN_{c}=1/\alpha colors, a color configuration a=(a1,…,aN)a=(a_{1},\ldots,a_{N}) assigns N/NcN/N_{c} particles to each color, and Sc​(a)S_{c}(a) denotes the set of particles of color cc. In terms of the spinor products wi​jw_{ij} of Sec. S1.1, the three wavefunctions read

Ψs\displaystyle\Psi_{\rm s} =∏i<jwi​j1/2​Ji​j​∑asgn⁡(a)​Pf​[ϵai​aj​w¯i​j 2​|wi​j|−1]​∏c∏i<j∈Sc​(a)w¯i​j​|wi​j|−1,\displaystyle=\prod_{i<j}w_{ij}^{1/2}J_{ij}\sum_{a}\mathrm{sgn}(a)\,\mathrm{Pf}\!\left[\epsilon_{a_{i}a_{j}}\,\bar{w}_{ij}^{\,2}|w_{ij}|^{-1}\right]\prod_{c}\prod_{i<j\in S_{c}(a)}\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-1}, (S39)
ΨSU⁡(2)\displaystyle\Psi_{\rm SU(2)} =∏i<jwi​j1/2​Ji​j​∑asgn⁡(a)​Pf​[ϵai​aj​ϵsi​sj​w¯i​j​|wi​j|−1]​∏c∏i<j∈Sc​(a)w¯i​j​|wi​j|−1,\displaystyle=\prod_{i<j}w_{ij}^{1/2}J_{ij}\sum_{a}\mathrm{sgn}(a)\,\mathrm{Pf}\!\left[\epsilon_{a_{i}a_{j}}\epsilon_{s_{i}s_{j}}\,\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-1}\right]\prod_{c}\prod_{i<j\in S_{c}(a)}\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-1}, (S40)
ΨSU⁡(3)\displaystyle\Psi_{\rm SU(3)} =∏i<jwi​j1/3Ji​j∑asgn(a)Pf[σi​jw¯i​j|wi​j|−2/3]∏c∏i<j∈Sc​(a)w¯i​j|wi​j|−2/3,\displaystyle=\prod_{i<j}w_{ij}^{1/3}J_{ij}\sum_{a}\mathrm{sgn}(a)\,\mathrm{Pf}\!\left[\sigma_{ij}\,\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-2/3}\right]\prod_{c}\prod_{i<j\in S_{c}(a)}\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-2/3}, (S41)

for spinless semions, SU(2) semions with spins sis_{i}, and SU(3) anyons with flavors bib_{i} at θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3. Here σi​j=∑A=13ϵA​ai​aj​ϵA​bi​bj\sigma_{ij}=\sum_{A=1}^{3}\epsilon_{Aa_{i}a_{j}}\epsilon_{Ab_{i}b_{j}} locks the colors of each Cooper pair to its flavors, Ji​jJ_{ij} is the long-range Jastrow factor of Eq. (S48), and sgn⁡(a)\mathrm{sgn}(a) is the sign of the permutation that groups the particles by color. The first product carries the anyon statistics, the Pfaffian pairs the holons of each coloring, and the last product, over same-color pairs, is the contact-corrected integer quantum Hall factor of χ\chi. Below we abbreviate the pair function as ui​j=w¯i​j​|wi​j|−2​αu_{ij}=\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-2\alpha} and the χ\chi factor as Ua=∏c∏i<j∈Sc​(a)ui​jU_{a}=\prod_{c}\prod_{i<j\in S_{c}(a)}u_{ij}, as in the main text.

Holon flux and shift sector.

In the CB gauge, the auxiliary wavefunction of Eq. (S21) sees 2​QΦ=qb​g−α⁡(N−1)2Q_{\Phi}=q_{bg}-\alpha(N-1) flux quanta (Sec. S1.1). For each coloring the auxiliary wavefunction is a product of the wavefunction for χa\chi_{a} and the holon ψa​b\psi_{ab}, so their fluxes add, 2​Qχ+2​Qψ=2​QΦ2Q_{\chi}+2Q_{\psi}=2Q_{\Phi}. Each color of χ\chi fills the reversed lowest level with N/NcN/N_{c} particles. This requires |2​Qχ|+1=N/Nc|2Q_{\chi}|+1=N/N_{c} with 2​Qχ<02Q_{\chi}<0, so 2​Qχ=1−N/Nc2Q_{\chi}=1-N/N_{c}. With Nc=1/αN_{c}=1/\alpha,

2​Qψ=2​QΦ−2​Qχ=qb​g−1+α.2Q_{\psi}=2Q_{\Phi}-2Q_{\chi}=q_{bg}-1+\alpha. (S42)

The integer quantum Hall factor of χ\chi cancels the extensive part −α​N-\alpha N of the statistical flux. Because the holon orbitals are single valued, 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} must be an integer. The color states therefore exist only for qb​g∈ℤ+1−αq_{bg}\in\mathbb{Z}+1-\alpha, that is, for half-integer qb​gq_{bg} for semions and for qb​g∈ℤ+23q_{bg}\in\mathbb{Z}+\frac{2}{3} at θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3.

The pairing channel then fixes the qb​gq_{bg} sector. We use the standard convention of Sec. S4.4: the pair orbital wi​jℓψw_{ij}^{\,\ell_{\psi}}, like zi​jℓψz_{ij}^{\,\ell_{\psi}} on the plane, has relative angular momentum ℓψ\ell_{\psi}, so an antiholomorphic pair orbital has ℓψ<0\ell_{\psi}<0. Since the pair orbital must transform like a holon orbital in each argument, 2​Qψ=ℓψ2Q_{\psi}=\ell_{\psi} and qb​g=1−α+ℓψq_{bg}=1-\alpha+\ell_{\psi}. The exchange parity required by the color and flavor tensors selects ℓψ\ell_{\psi}. For spinless semions, the color singlet pairing is in the d−i​dd-id channel, which requires qb​g=−3/2q_{bg}=-3/2. For SU(2) semions, the color-singlet, spin-singlet pairing is in the p−i​pp-ip channel, which requires qb​g=−1/2q_{bg}=-1/2. Both semion states require an even NN. For SU(3) anyons with θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3, bib_{i} is the physical flavor, and the symmetric tensor σi​j\sigma_{ij} enforces a color-antisymmetric, flavor-antisymmetric pairing in the p−i​pp-ip channel, ℓψ=−1\ell_{\psi}=-1, which requires qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3. Here NN is a multiple of six so that the three colors have equal populations and all holons can pair. The gauge-invariant condensate combines three holon pairs and carries the charge of six anyons.

S3.1 Fixing the radial power at contact

In local planar coordinates zi​j=r​ei​φz_{ij}=r\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\varphi}, the regular two-anyon solutions with relative angular momentum ℓ=α\ell=\alpha and ℓ=α−1\ell=\alpha-1 are zi​jαz_{ij}^{\alpha} and z¯i​j 1−α=r1−α​ei⁡(α−1)​φ\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,1-\alpha}=r^{1-\alpha}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\alpha-1)\varphi}. Exchange symmetry restricts two anyons of the same flavor to ℓ∈α+2​ℤ\ell\in\alpha+2\mathbb{Z}, so the ℓ=α−1\ell=\alpha-1 channel is allowed only for different flavors. In one coloring of Eqs. (S39)–(S41), a pair can receive an antiholomorphic factor from the Pfaffian, if the two anyons are Cooper partners, which requires different colors, or from UaU_{a}, if they have the same color. Otherwise it enters only through the common factor zi​jαz_{ij}^{\alpha}. The radial power |zi​j|−2​α|z_{ij}|^{-2\alpha} in ui​ju_{ij} makes each antiholomorphic factor a regular two-anyon solution. Contact regularity fixes this power only as r→0r\to 0, and our variational choice continues it as a pure power at all separations.

Spinless semions, Eq. (S39). All anyons have the same flavor. A Cooper pair carries w¯i​j​ui​j\bar{w}_{ij}u_{ij} from the Pfaffian and enters as zi​jα​z¯i​j​ui​j=z¯i​j 2−αz_{ij}^{\alpha}\bar{z}_{ij}u_{ij}=\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,2-\alpha}, the regular solution with ℓ=α−2\ell=\alpha-2. The factor ui​ju_{ij} of a same-color pair in UaU_{a} does not produce the ℓ=α−1\ell=\alpha-1 channel, as shown below, so every pair approaches as a combination of zi​j1/2z_{ij}^{1/2} and z¯i​j 3/2\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,3/2}.

SU(2) semions, Eq. (S40). The Pfaffian pairs only opposite spins, and a Cooper pair enters as zi​j1/2​ui​j=z¯i​j 1/2z_{ij}^{1/2}u_{ij}=\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,1/2}. A same-color pair of opposite spins carries the same factor from UaU_{a}. Two opposite spins therefore approach as a combination of zi​j1/2z_{ij}^{1/2} and z¯i​j 1/2\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,1/2}, whereas two equal spins approach as zi​j1/2z_{ij}^{1/2}.

SU(3) anyons, Eq. (S41). Since σi​j=0\sigma_{ij}=0 for bi=bjb_{i}=b_{j}, the Pfaffian pairs only different flavors, and a Cooper pair enters as zi​j1/3​ui​j=z¯i​j 2/3z_{ij}^{1/3}u_{ij}=\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,2/3}. A same-color pair of different flavors carries the same factor from UaU_{a}. Two anyons of different flavors therefore approach as a combination of zi​j1/3z_{ij}^{1/3} and z¯i​j 2/3\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,2/3}, and two anyons of the same flavor approach as zi​j1/3z_{ij}^{1/3}.

Same-flavor contact. For one coloring, let MM be the antisymmetric N×NN\times N matrix inside the Pfaffian, with rows and columns labeled by the anyons, for example Mk​l=σk​l​uk​lM_{kl}=\sigma_{kl}u_{kl} in Eq. (S41). Its Pfaffian Pf​M=∑πsgn⁡(π)​∏(k,l)∈πMk​l\mathrm{Pf}M=\sum_{\pi}\mathrm{sgn}(\pi)\prod_{(k,l)\in\pi}M_{kl} runs over all pairings π\pi of the NN anyons into Cooper pairs, and (Pf​M)2=detM(\mathrm{Pf}M)^{2}=\det M. Two anyons ii and jj of the same flavor can carry z¯i​j 1−α\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,1-\alpha} only through ui​ju_{ij} in UaU_{a}, when they also share a color: in Eqs. (S40) and (S41) anyons of the same flavor are never Cooper partners, and a Cooper pair of spinless semions gives z¯i​j 2−α\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,2-\alpha}. With identical color and flavor labels, Mi​j=0M_{ij}=0, and the color and flavor tensors in rows ii and jj coincide, for example σi​k=σj​k\sigma_{ik}=\sigma_{jk} for every kk. The two rows then differ only through ui​ku_{ik} and uj​ku_{jk}, which become equal as zi→zjz_{i}\to z_{j}. Exchanging the positions of ii and jj therefore amounts to exchanging rows i,ji,j and columns i,ji,j of MM, which reverses the sign of the Pfaffian. The Pfaffian is thus odd in the relative coordinate and vanishes linearly, as a combination of zi​jz_{ij} and z¯i​j\bar{z}_{ij}. Multiplied by zi​jα​ui​j=z¯i​j 1−αz_{ij}^{\alpha}u_{ij}=\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,1-\alpha}, it gives z¯i​j 1−α​zi​j\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,1-\alpha}z_{ij} and z¯i​j 2−α\bar{z}_{ij}^{\,2-\alpha}, which lie in the allowed channels ℓ=α\ell=\alpha and ℓ=α−2\ell=\alpha-2 and vanish at least as r2−αr^{2-\alpha}. The leading same-flavor behavior is therefore zi​jαz_{ij}^{\alpha}, from the colorings in which the two anyons have different colors.

S3.2 Flavor symmetry and projection

The above wavefunction for the SU(3) anyons with θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3 actually weakly breaks the SU(3) flavor symmetry. A flavor rotation g∈SU⁡(3)g\in{\rm SU(3)} acts on Eq. (S41) only through σi​j\sigma_{ij}, which it replaces by σi​j​(W)=∑A,BϵA​ai​aj​WA​B​ϵB​bi​bj\sigma_{ij}(W)=\sum_{A,B}\epsilon_{Aa_{i}a_{j}}W_{AB}\epsilon_{Bb_{i}b_{j}} with W=g−1W=g^{-1}. The same-color factor in UaU_{a} depends on the individual color labels, so Eq. (S41) is not exactly invariant. The exact flavor singlet is the Haar average over the locking matrix,

ΨSU⁡(3)(0)=∫SU⁡(3)d​W​ΨSU⁡(3)|σi​j→σi​j​(W).\Psi_{\rm SU(3)}^{(0)}=\int_{\rm SU(3)}dW\;\Psi_{\rm SU(3)}\Big|_{\sigma_{ij}\to\sigma_{ij}(W)}. (S43)

If UaU_{a} were a color singlet, as the filled lowest levels ∏c∏i<j∈Sc​(a)w¯i​j\prod_{c}\prod_{i<j\in S_{c}(a)}\bar{w}_{ij} without the radial power are, this average would return Eq. (S41) unchanged. The integrand is a polynomial of degree N/2N/2 in WW. We use Eq. (S41) without the projection, because the non-singlet admixture it would remove is small: it vanishes at N=6N=6 and is about 0.15% at N=12N=12, according to the Casimir test below.

A simpler construction restores the symmetry exactly by switching color indices instead of averaging over WW. Writing the radial part of UaU_{a} as ∏i<j[1+(fi​j−1)​δai​aj]\prod_{i<j}[1+(f_{ij}-1)\delta_{a_{i}a_{j}}] with fi​j=|wi​j|−2​αf_{ij}=|w_{ij}|^{-2\alpha}, the breaking comes from the color-diagonal δai​aj\delta_{a_{i}a_{j}}, which is not invariant under color rotations. We replace it by the color-symmetric projector (1+Pi​jc)/2(1+P^{c}_{ij})/2, where Pi​jcP^{c}_{ij} switches the color indices of anyons ii and jj. This gives the pair factor

Fi​j=1+fi​j2+fi​j−12​Pi​jc,F_{ij}=\frac{1+f_{ij}}{2}+\frac{f_{ij}-1}{2}\,P^{c}_{ij}, (S44)

which equals fi​jf_{ij} for a same-color pair, where Pi​jc=1P^{c}_{ij}=1, and commutes with color rotations, so the state is an exact flavor singlet. Because the χ\chi partons are fermions, Pk​lcP^{c}_{kl} acting on the χ\chi factor equals minus the exchange of the coordinates of kk and ll in it. Applying 1+∑k<l(Fk​l−1)1+\sum_{k<l}(F_{kl}-1) to the plain χ\chi factor V¯a=∏c∏i<j∈Sc​(a)w¯i​j\bar{V}_{a}=\prod_{c}\prod_{i<j\in S_{c}(a)}\bar{w}_{ij} gives the flavor-symmetric wavefunction

ΨSU⁡(3)sym=∏i<jwi​j1/3Ji​j∑asgn(a)Pf[σi​jw¯i​j|wi​j|−2/3][V¯a+∑k<lfk​l−12(V¯a−V¯a|k↔l)],\Psi_{\rm SU(3)}^{\rm sym}=\prod_{i<j}w_{ij}^{1/3}J_{ij}\sum_{a}\mathrm{sgn}(a)\,\mathrm{Pf}\!\left[\sigma_{ij}\,\bar{w}_{ij}|w_{ij}|^{-2/3}\right]\Big[\bar{V}_{a}+\sum_{k<l}\frac{f_{kl}-1}{2}\big(\bar{V}_{a}-\bar{V}_{a}\big|_{k\leftrightarrow l}\big)\Big], (S45)

where V¯a|k↔l\bar{V}_{a}|_{k\leftrightarrow l} is V¯a\bar{V}_{a} with the positions of anyons kk and ll exchanged. For a same-color pair V¯a|k↔l=−V¯a\bar{V}_{a}|_{k\leftrightarrow l}=-\bar{V}_{a}, so the bracket multiplies V¯a\bar{V}_{a} by fk​lf_{kl}, as UaU_{a} does. We keep the radial factor within the first neighbor shell, fk​l=(dk​l/1.5​a0)−2​α​sk​lf_{kl}=(d_{kl}/1.5a_{0})^{-2\alpha s_{kl}} with sk​l=[1−(dk​l/1.5​a0)2]2s_{kl}=[1-(d_{kl}/1.5a_{0})^{2}]^{2} for dk​l<1.5​a0d_{kl}<1.5a_{0} and fk​l=1f_{kl}=1 otherwise. We also use the additive form instead of the product of the Fk​lF_{kl}, which keeps the number of terms linear in the number of close pairs. Since V¯a\bar{V}_{a} contributes |wi​j||w_{ij}| for each distant same-color pair, Ji​jJ_{ij} uses γ=1/3+(N−2)/[3​(N−1)]\gamma=1/3+(N-2)/[3(N-1)]. Equation (S45) is the flavor-covariant state whose energies are quoted in Sec. S5.3. A plain average over permutations of the color labels would not help, since these permutations act on σi​j\sigma_{ij} as a finite subgroup of the WW in Eq. (S43) and Eq. (S41) is already invariant under them, so the average would return it unchanged, non-singlet admixture included.

This problem does not arise for SU(2) semions. In Eq. (S40) the spin tensor ϵsi​sj\epsilon_{s_{i}s_{j}} shares no index with the color tensor, so every term of the Pfaffian is a product of spin singlets whatever the color factor, and the state is an exact spin singlet. In the SU(3) state, by contrast, σi​j\sigma_{ij} ties the flavor index of each Cooper pair to a color index, so flavor invariance relies on a color-singlet color factor.

Casimir test.

We measure the flavor symmetry with the quadratic Casimir of the total flavor rotation, C2=∑iC2(i)+2​∑i<j𝐓i⋅𝐓jC_{2}=\sum_{i}C_{2}^{(i)}+2\sum_{i<j}\mathbf{T}_{i}\cdot\mathbf{T}_{j}, where 𝐓i\mathbf{T}_{i} are the SU(3) generators acting on the flavor of anyon ii. In the fundamental representation C2(i)=4/3C_{2}^{(i)}=4/3 and 2​𝐓i⋅𝐓j=Pi​j−1/32\mathbf{T}_{i}\cdot\mathbf{T}_{j}=P_{ij}-1/3, where Pi​jP_{ij} exchanges the flavors of anyons ii and jj. With N/3N/3 anyons of each flavor, Pi​j=1P_{ij}=1 for the N⁡(N−3)/6N(N-3)/6 pairs of equal flavor, so C2=N+∑i<j,bi≠bjPi​jC_{2}=N+\sum_{i<j,\,b_{i}\neq b_{j}}P_{ij}. In the CB gauge Φ\Phi is symmetric under exchanging both the positions and the flavors of two anyons, so Pi​j​Φ​(R)=Φ⁡(R(i​j))P_{ij}\Phi(R)=\Phi(R^{(ij)}), where R(i​j)R^{(ij)} is the configuration RR with the positions of ii and jj exchanged. The statistical and Jastrow factors do not depend on the flavors, so

D⁡(R)≡[C2​Ψ]​(R)Ψ⁡(R)=N+∑i<j,bi≠bjΦ⁡(R(i​j))Φ⁡(R).D(R)\equiv\frac{[C_{2}\Psi](R)}{\Psi(R)}=N+\sum_{i<j,\,b_{i}\neq b_{j}}\frac{\Phi(R^{(ij)})}{\Phi(R)}. (S46)

A flavor singlet has C2=0C_{2}=0 and therefore D⁡(R)=0D(R)=0 at every configuration RR. In general, we decompose Ψ\Psi into components Ψρ\Psi_{\rho} in the irreducible representations ρ\rho of SU(3), with weights pρp_{\rho}. Averages over |Ψ|2|\Psi|^{2} then give ⟨D⟩=∑ρC2​(ρ)​pρ\langle D\rangle=\sum_{\rho}C_{2}(\rho)\,p_{\rho} and ⟨|D|2⟩=∑ρC2​(ρ)2​pρ\langle|D|^{2}\rangle=\sum_{\rho}C_{2}(\rho)^{2}p_{\rho}. Equation (S41) is invariant under every permutation of the three flavors, because the same permutation of the colors in the sum over colorings compensates it, and we confirm this numerically. Its components are zero-weight states, with N/3N/3 anyons of each flavor, and the zero-weight states of the octet and of the decuplets contain no state invariant under these permutations. These representations therefore cannot appear, and every admixture has C2≥8C_{2}\geq 8, the value of the 27-dimensional representation. Both ⟨D⟩/8\langle D\rangle/8 and ⟨|D|2⟩/64\langle|D|^{2}\rangle/64 thus bound the total non-singlet weight from above, and both equal it for a pure 27-plet admixture. Equation (S41) gives |D|<10−14|D|<10^{-14} at N=6N=6. At N=12N=12, 768 configurations give ⟨D⟩/8=0.16​(7)%\langle D\rangle/8=0.16(7)\% and ⟨|D|2⟩/64=0.15​(2)%\langle|D|^{2}\rangle/64=0.15(2)\%, consistent with a 27-plet admixture of about 0.15%.

S3.3 Fixing the long-distance correlations

The pair amplitudes also contribute powers of distance to the modulus of the wavefunction. For SU(2) semions |ui​j|=1|u_{ij}|=1, so the only such power is the common |wi​j|1/2|w_{ij}|^{1/2}, and |Ψ|2|\Psi|^{2} contains

∏i<j|wi​j|∝exp⁡(∑i<jln⁡di​j).\prod_{i<j}|w_{ij}|\propto\exp\Big(\sum_{i<j}\ln d_{ij}\Big).

This is the Boltzmann weight of a classical two-dimensional plasma in which all particles repel logarithmically. For |Ψ|2∝exp[−∑i<jv(di​j)]|\Psi|^{2}\propto\exp[-\sum_{i<j}v(d_{ij})], the random-phase approximation of this classical fluid, which gives the exact small-qq behavior for a long-range vv, yields

S⁡(q)=11+n​v~​(q),S(q)=\frac{1}{1+n\tilde{v}(q)}, (S47)

where v~​(q)\tilde{v}(q) is the two-dimensional Fourier transform of vv. The logarithm v=−ln⁡dv=-\ln d has v~=2​π/q2\tilde{v}=2\pi/q^{2}, so S⁡(q)=q2/(q2+2​π​n)≃q2​a02/2​πS(q)=q^{2}/(q^{2}+2\pi n)\simeq q^{2}a_{0}^{2}/2\pi with a0=n−1/2a_{0}=n^{-1/2}. The plasma screens perfectly, and its density is incompressible. A superfluid with a sound mode instead has S⁡(q)≃s​qS(q)\simeq s\,q at small qq, which by Eq. (S47) requires v~∝1/q\tilde{v}\propto 1/q, that is, a 1/d1/d tail of vv [74]. We remove the mean long-distance power and supply this tail with a flavor-independent Jastrow factor

Ji​j=(1+di​j2a02)−γ/2exp[−λ​a0di​j2+a02].J_{ij}=\left(1+\frac{d_{ij}^{2}}{a_{0}^{2}}\right)^{-\gamma/2}\exp\!\left[-\frac{\lambda a_{0}}{\sqrt{d_{ij}^{2}+a_{0}^{2}}}\right]. (S48)

Both factors are smooth at contact. The first contributes di​j−γd_{ij}^{-\gamma} at long distance and cancels the mean power. The second adds v=2​λ​a0/dv=2\lambda a_{0}/d, with v~=4​π​λ​a0/q\tilde{v}=4\pi\lambda a_{0}/q, so that Eq. (S47) gives S⁡(q)≃q​a0/(4​π​λ)S(q)\simeq qa_{0}/(4\pi\lambda) at small qq.

We fix λ\lambda by matching this slope to the phonon of the superfluid. The ideal anyon gas has no length scale other than a0a_{0}, so its energy per particle in the thermodynamic limit has the form E/N=e∞​π​ℏ2​n/mE/N=e_{\infty}\pi\hbar^{2}n/m. The energy density e∞​π​ℏ2​n2/me_{\infty}\pi\hbar^{2}n^{2}/m gives the chemical potential μ=2​π​e∞​ℏ2​n/m\mu=2\pi e_{\infty}\hbar^{2}n/m, and the compressibility gives the sound speed through m​c2=n​∂μ/∂n=2​π​e∞​ℏ2​n/mmc^{2}=n\,\partial\mu/\partial n=2\pi e_{\infty}\hbar^{2}n/m. At small qq the phonon exhausts the ff-sum rule ∫d​ω​ℏ​ω​S​(q,ω)=ℏ2​q2/2​m\int d\omega\,\hbar\omega\,S(q,\omega)=\hbar^{2}q^{2}/2m, which gives the Feynman relation S⁡(q)=ℏ​q/(2​m​c)S(q)=\hbar q/(2mc). Hence s=ℏ/(2​m​c)=a0/(2​2​π​e∞)s=\hbar/(2mc)=a_{0}/(2\sqrt{2\pi e_{\infty}}), and equating it to a0/(4​π​λ)a_{0}/(4\pi\lambda) gives

λ=e∞/2​π.\lambda=\sqrt{e_{\infty}/2\pi}.

We take e∞e_{\infty} from independently optimized states of the same phase, so that λ\lambda is fixed before the trial state is evaluated: e∞=0.784e_{\infty}=0.784 and 0.5410.541 from the CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 states of spinless and SU(2) semions (Table S2), and e∞=0.492e_{\infty}=0.492 for SU(3) anyons from a preliminary extrapolation of the analytical state with a trained Jastrow factor and backflow, close to the 0.498​(1)0.498(1) of the optimized color superconductor.

For SU(2) semions the common power gives γ=1/2\gamma=1/2. For spinless semions the extra w¯i​j\bar{w}_{ij} in each Cooper pair adds one power per particle. Distributed over its N−1N-1 partners this gives γ=1/2+1/(N−1)\gamma=1/2+1/(N-1). For SU(3), each particle has N/3−1N/3-1 same-color partners and one Cooper partner, each contributing |ui​j|=|wi​j|1/3|u_{ij}|=|w_{ij}|^{1/3}. Including the common 1/31/3 gives γ=1/3+N/[9​(N−1)]\gamma=1/3+N/[9(N-1)]. The values of λ\lambda used for spinless semions, SU(2) semions and SU(3) anyons are 0.3530.353, 0.2930.293 and 0.2800.280, respectively.

The energies without Ji​jJ_{ij}, which need no input, lie only 0.5–2% higher: e∞=0.550​(3)e_{\infty}=0.550(3) instead of 0.5405​(16)0.5405(16) for SU(2) semions (Sec. S5.1), e∞=0.509​(1)e_{\infty}=0.509(1) from the four sizes in Sec. S5.3 instead of 0.498​(3)0.498(3) for SU(3) anyons, and E/N=0.8007​(30)E/N=0.8007(30) instead of 0.7963​(15)0.7963(15) at N=24N=24 for spinless semions. Fixing λ\lambda from the state without Ji​jJ_{ij} would give λ=0.296\lambda=0.296 and 0.2850.285 for SU(2) semions and SU(3) anyons, within 2% of the values above. The construction can therefore be made self-contained, with e∞e_{\infty} estimated from the ansatz without Ji​jJ_{ij}; we have not re-evaluated the energies with these slightly different values of λ\lambda.

S4 Low-energy effective theories

S4.1 Flux attachment as a Chern–Simons theory

Writing the anyon wavefunction as Ψ=∏i<j(zi​j/|zi​j|)αs​Φ\Psi=\prod_{i<j}(z_{ij}/|z_{ij}|)^{\alpha_{s}}\Phi isolates the statistical factor ei​αs​∑i<jθi​j\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\alpha_{s}\sum_{i<j}\theta_{ij}}, where θi​j=arg⁡zi​j\theta_{ij}=\arg z_{ij}. Acting on this factor with the kinetic operator gives

ℋΨ=ei​αs​∑i<jθi​j∑iℏ22​m[−i∇i−𝐀(𝐫i)−𝐚(𝐫i)]2Φ,𝐚(𝐫i)=−αs∑j≠iz^×𝐫i​jri​j2,\mathcal{H}\Psi=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\alpha_{s}\sum_{i<j}\theta_{ij}}\sum_{i}\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\bigl[-\mathrm{i}\nabla_{i}-\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{r}_{i})-\mathbf{a}(\mathbf{r}_{i})\bigr]^{2}\Phi,\qquad\mathbf{a}(\mathbf{r}_{i})=-\alpha_{s}\sum_{j\neq i}\frac{\hat{z}\times\mathbf{r}_{ij}}{r_{ij}^{2}}, (S49)

so Φ\Phi describes particles that carry −αs-\alpha_{s} flux quanta of 𝐚\mathbf{a}, ∇×𝐚=−2παs∑jδ2(𝐫−𝐫j)\nabla\times\mathbf{a}=-2\pi\alpha_{s}\sum_{j}\delta^{2}(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_{j}). In field theory, we introduce aμa_{\mu} as a U(1) gauge field with a self Chern-Simons (CS) term,

ℒ=ℒΦ​[a]+14​π​αs​a​d​a,\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\Phi}[a]+\frac{1}{4\pi\alpha_{s}}\,a\,da, (S50)

The equation of motion by varying a0a_{0} gives the internal flux b=−2​π​αs​ρb=-2\pi\alpha_{s}\rho. Coupling every flavor to the same field aa implements the flavor-independent statistics. At mean field, b¯=−2​π​αs​n\bar{b}=-2\pi\alpha_{s}n. The signed filling ν∗=2πn/b¯=−1/αs\nu^{*}=2\pi n/\bar{b}=-1/\alpha_{s} therefore gives −1/α-1/\alpha for CBs and 1/(1−α)1/(1-\alpha) for CFs. Each variational family below is a mean-field state of Eq. (S50), or of its parton representation. We use the notation X​d​Y=ϵμ​ν​λ​Xμ​∂νYλX\,dY=\epsilon^{\mu\nu\lambda}X_{\mu}\partial_{\nu}Y_{\lambda}.

Parent FCI.

If the anyons are the quasiparticles of a parent FCI with topological order U(1)m, m=1/αm=1/\alpha, the CB form of Eq. (S50) is its Chern–Simons theory, and the electromagnetic field AcA_{c} couples to the flux of aa,

ℒ=ℒB​[a]+m4​π​a​d​a+12​π​Ac​d​a.\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{B}[a]+\frac{m}{4\pi}a\,da+\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,da. (S51)

Integrating out aa gives σx​y=−1me2/h\sigma_{xy}=-\frac{1}{m}\,e^{2}/h, and the Gauss law gives the anyon charge q=−1/mq=-1/m (in units of ee, as all charges below).

The CF gauge follows from the exact transmutation of a boson into a fermion bound to one flux quantum, ℒB​[X]=ℒF​[X+γ]−14​π​γ​d​γ\mathcal{L}_{B}[X]=\mathcal{L}_{F}[X+\gamma]-\frac{1}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma: the CFs couple to u=a+γu=a+\gamma and see αs=α−1\alpha_{s}=\alpha-1. For semions (m=2m=2) the unimodular change of variables to uu and w=2​a+γw=2a+\gamma gives 24​π​a​d​a−14​π​γ​d​γ=−24​π​u​d​u+14​π​w​d​w\frac{2}{4\pi}a\,da-\frac{1}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma=-\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du+\frac{1}{4\pi}w\,dw, so ww decouples from the matter, and integrating it out leaves the CF form of Eq. (S50) with the parent FCI (uu is the CF-gauge aa of the main text),

ℒ=ℒF​[u]−24​π​u​d​u−12​π​Ac​d​u−14​π​Ac​d​Ac.\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{F}[u]-\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du-\frac{1}{4\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c}. (S52)

At θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3 the CF level 1/αs=−3/21/\alpha_{s}=-3/2 is not an integer, and we keep aa and γ\gamma separate (Sec. S4.3).

S4.2 Semions: superfluid of pairs

At ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2, the CFs fill two Landau levels under the effective magnetic field b¯\bar{b}. Integrating out these gapped fermions produces their Hall response together with a Maxwell term set by the CF cyclotron gap, which combines with Eq. (S52) to give

ℒ=24​π​u​d​u−24​π​u​d​u−12​π​Ac​d​u−14​π​Ac​d​Ac+ϵ2​𝐞2−12​μ​b2=−12​π​Ac​d​u−14​π​Ac​d​Ac+ϵ2​𝐞2−12​μ​b2.\begin{split}\mathcal{L}&=\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du-\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du-\frac{1}{4\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}\mathbf{e}^{2}-\frac{1}{2\mu}b^{2}\\ &=-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du-\frac{1}{4\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}\mathbf{e}^{2}-\frac{1}{2\mu}b^{2}.\end{split} (S53)

The exact cancellation of the Chern–Simons term leaves a pure Maxwell field in 2+1 dimensions, which is dual to a compact scalar σ\sigma through 12​π​ϵμ​ν​λ​∂νuλ∝∂μσ\frac{1}{2\pi}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\lambda}\partial_{\nu}u_{\lambda}\propto\partial^{\mu}\sigma. The coupling −12​π​Ac​d​u-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du identifies σ\sigma as the phase of a superfluid [9, 8], whose condensed boson consists of a pair of semions. For SU(2) semions, the spin sector also has a quantized Hall response. A probe AsA_{s} coupled to Sz=±12S_{z}=\pm\frac{1}{2} gives 14​π​∑±(u±12​As)​d​(u±12​As)=24​π​u​d​u+18​π​As​d​As\frac{1}{4\pi}\sum_{\pm}\big(u\pm\frac{1}{2}A_{s}\big)d\big(u\pm\frac{1}{2}A_{s}\big)=\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du+\frac{1}{8\pi}A_{s}\,dA_{s}, which reproduces Eq. (S53) in the charge sector and leaves the spin Hall term 18​π​As​d​As\frac{1}{8\pi}A_{s}\,dA_{s} for the gapped spin sector.

The pairs in the wavefunction.

On the plane, with ℓ∗=(πn)−1/2\ell^{*}=(\pi n)^{-1/2} and G=∏ie−|zi|2/4ℓ∗2G=\prod_{i}\mathrm{e}^{-|z_{i}|^{2}/4\ell^{*2}}, the semion states are ΦF=χ2​G\Phi_{F}=\chi_{2}G with χ2=det[zik|z¯i​zik]\chi_{2}=\det[z_{i}^{k}\,|\,\bar{z}_{i}z_{i}^{k}], k=0,…,N/2−1k=0,\ldots,N/2-1 (spinless), and ΦF=Δ⁡(z)​Δ​(w)​G\Phi_{F}=\Delta(z)\Delta(w)G [SU(2), with zz (ww) the up (down) coordinates and Δ⁡(z)=∏i<j(zi−zj)\Delta(z)=\prod_{i<j}(z_{i}-z_{j})]. We follow one pair whose members sit at RR and R+εR+\varepsilon, and denote the other N−2N-2 coordinates by Z′Z^{\prime}.

SU(2) semions. With the up particle z1z_{1} and the down particle w1w_{1} both at RR, each Vandermonde factorizes, Δ(z)=±∏k(zk−R)Δ(z′)\Delta(z)=\pm\prod_{k}(z_{k}-R)\,\Delta(z^{\prime}) and Δ(w)=±∏k(wk−R)Δ(w′)\Delta(w)=\pm\prod_{k}(w_{k}-R)\,\Delta(w^{\prime}), with the products over the remaining up and down particles, and the two Gaussians combine into e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}. Writing zkz_{k} for the coordinate of a remaining particle of either spin,

ΦF(R,R,Z′)=±e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2∏k∈Z′(zk−R)ΦF(N−2)(Z′).\Phi_{F}(R,R,Z^{\prime})=\pm\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}\prod_{k\in Z^{\prime}}(z_{k}-R)\,\Phi_{F}^{(N-2)}(Z^{\prime}). (S54)

An up–down pair has no Pauli zero, so this amplitude is the ε→0\varepsilon\to 0 limit.

Spinless semions. Two members of the same species vanish at contact, so we expand to first order in ε\varepsilon. Subtracting the row of the member at RR from that of the member at R+εR+\varepsilon leaves (k​ε​Rk−1|ε¯​Rk+k​ε​R¯​Rk−1)(k\varepsilon R^{k-1}\,|\,\bar{\varepsilon}R^{k}+k\varepsilon\bar{R}R^{k-1}), so χ2​(R,R+ε,Z′)=ε¯​A+ε​B+O⁡(|ε|2)\chi_{2}(R,R+\varepsilon,Z^{\prime})=\bar{\varepsilon}A+\varepsilon B+O(|\varepsilon|^{2}). In AA the first two rows are (Rk|R¯​Rk)(R^{k}\,|\,\bar{R}R^{k}) and (0|Rk)(0\,|\,R^{k}), and subtracting R¯\bar{R} times the second from the first turns them into (Rk| 0)(R^{k}\,|\,0) and (0|Rk)(0\,|\,R^{k}). If another particle sits at zk=Rz_{k}=R, its row (Rk|z¯k​Rk)(R^{k}\,|\,\bar{z}_{k}R^{k}) is a combination of these two, so AA vanishes linearly in zk−Rz_{k}-R and contains ∏k∈Z′(zk−R)\prod_{k\in Z^{\prime}}(z_{k}-R). The remaining factor is antisymmetric in Z′Z^{\prime} and lies in the two lowest LLs with one orbital fewer each, which the N−2N-2 fermions fill in a unique way, and a Laplace expansion along the first two rows fixes the prefactor: A=±∏k∈Z′(zk−R)χ2(N−2)(Z′)A=\pm\prod_{k\in Z^{\prime}}(z_{k}-R)\,\chi_{2}^{(N-2)}(Z^{\prime}) exactly, the analog of Eq. (S54). The pair therefore condenses in the ε¯\bar{\varepsilon} channel.

Cancellation of the vortex. In the anyon wavefunction the two members carry the statistical factor [(zk−R)/|zk−R|]αs[(z_{k}-R)/|z_{k}-R|]^{\alpha_{s}} with every other particle, which gives ∏k[(zk−R)/|zk−R|]2​αs=∏k(zk−R)−1​|zk−R|\prod_{k}[(z_{k}-R)/|z_{k}-R|]^{2\alpha_{s}}=\prod_{k}(z_{k}-R)^{-1}|z_{k}-R| at αs=−1/2\alpha_{s}=-1/2. This removes the vortex ∏k(zk−R)\prod_{k}(z_{k}-R) and leaves

Ψ(pair at R;Z′)=ϕpair(ε)WR(Z′)Ψ(N−2)(Z′),WR=e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2∏k|zk−R|>0,\Psi(\text{pair at }R;Z^{\prime})=\phi_{\rm pair}(\varepsilon)\,W_{R}(Z^{\prime})\,\Psi^{(N-2)}(Z^{\prime}),\qquad W_{R}=\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}\prod_{k}|z_{k}-R|>0, (S55)

with ϕpair=(ε/|ε|)αs\phi_{\rm pair}=(\varepsilon/|\varepsilon|)^{\alpha_{s}} for SU(2) and (ε/|ε|)αs​ε¯(\varepsilon/|\varepsilon|)^{\alpha_{s}}\bar{\varepsilon} for spinless semions. The amplitude for the pair at RR is positive and nodeless, as in Feynman’s argument for bosons. For a uniform density, two-dimensional electrostatics gives ⟨∑kln⁡|zk−R|⟩=n​∫d2​r​ln⁡|𝐫−R|=π​n2​|R|2+const\langle\sum_{k}\ln|z_{k}-R|\rangle=n\int d^{2}r\,\ln|\mathbf{r}-R|=\frac{\pi n}{2}|R|^{2}+{\rm const}, which cancels the Gaussian e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2=e−πn|R|2/2\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}=\mathrm{e}^{-\pi n|R|^{2}/2}.

BCS form. For SU(2) semions, Cauchy’s identity

det[1zi−wj]=±Δ⁡(z)​Δ​(w)∏i,j(zi−wj)\det\Big[\frac{1}{z_{i}-w_{j}}\Big]=\pm\frac{\Delta(z)\Delta(w)}{\prod_{i,j}(z_{i}-w_{j})}

gives ΦF=±∏i,j(zi−wj)det[1/(zi−wj)]G\Phi_{F}=\pm\prod_{i,j}(z_{i}-w_{j})\,\det[1/(z_{i}-w_{j})]\,G. The determinant det[g⁡(zi−wj)]=∑Psgn⁡(P)​∏ig⁡(zi−wP⁡(i))\det[g(z_{i}-w_{j})]=\sum_{P}\mathrm{sgn}(P)\prod_{i}g(z_{i}-w_{P(i)}) with g⁡(z)=1/zg(z)=1/z is the component with N/2N/2 pairs of the BCS state exp⁡[∫d2​r​d2​r′​g​(𝐫−𝐫′)​c↑†​(𝐫)​c↓†​(𝐫′)]​|0⟩\exp[\int d^{2}r\,d^{2}r^{\prime}\,g(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}^{\prime})\,c^{\dagger}_{\uparrow}(\mathbf{r})c^{\dagger}_{\downarrow}(\mathbf{r}^{\prime})]|0\rangle. The remaining factor, ∏i,j(zi−wj)​G\prod_{i,j}(z_{i}-w_{j})\,G together with the statistical phases, vanishes only at contact and acts as a Jastrow factor. The SU(2) state is therefore a number-projected BCS state of up–down semion pairs with the CF pair function 1/(z−w)1/(z-w), times a Jastrow factor [95].

Pair coherence.

The pair density matrix ρ2​(R,R′)∝⟨WR​WR′⟩N−2\rho_{2}(R,R^{\prime})\propto\langle W_{R}W_{R^{\prime}}\rangle_{N-2} can be evaluated without a sign problem. In the bare state, the CF density is incompressible, with S⁡(q)=q2​ℓ∗2/2S(q)=q^{2}\ell^{*2}/2, so that ln⁡WR=∫ρ​ln⁡|𝐫−R|\ln W_{R}=\int\rho\ln|\mathbf{r}-R| has logarithmic correlations and C2=ρ2​(R,R′)/ρ2​(R,R)∝(ℓ∗/d)ν∗/2C_{2}=\rho_{2}(R,R^{\prime})/\rho_{2}(R,R)\propto(\ell^{*}/d)^{\nu^{*}/2} exhibits only algebraic pair order. True off-diagonal long-range order requires S⁡(q)∝qS(q)\propto q, which in a Jastrow description can be obtained by combining ∏i<j|wi​j|−1/2\prod_{i<j}|w_{ij}|^{-1/2}, which removes the logarithmic kernel, with a Reatto–Chester tail [74]. In our wavefunctions, the backflow and Jastrow factor modify these correlations so that the pair correlator approaches a plateau, indicating long-range pair order (Sec. S5.1).

S4.3 CF states at ν∗=3/2\nu^{*}=3/2: trion Fermi liquid

At α=1/3\alpha=1/3 the CFs couple to u=a+γu=a+\gamma (Sec. S4.1) and see b¯=4​π3​n\bar{b}=\frac{4\pi}{3}n. The lowest level is filled (density 2​n/32n/3) and the second holds n/3n/3, half filling. Integrating out the filled level gives 14​π​u​d​u\frac{1}{4\pi}u\,du. The second-level CFs are in the situation of electrons at ν=1/2\nu=1/2 [75]: attaching two more flux quanta through a field a~\tilde{a}, in the integer form 12​π​a~​d​g−24​π​g​d​g\frac{1}{2\pi}\tilde{a}\,dg-\frac{2}{4\pi}g\,dg (which gives 18​π​a~​d​a~\frac{1}{8\pi}\tilde{a}\,d\tilde{a} when gg is integrated out), makes the final fermions ff see zero average field,

ℒ=ℒf​[u+a~]+14​π​u​d​u+34​π​a​d​a−14​π​γ​d​γ+12​π​Ac​d​a+12​π​a~​d​g−24​π​g​d​g.\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{f}[u+\tilde{a}]+\frac{1}{4\pi}u\,du+\frac{3}{4\pi}a\,da-\frac{1}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma+\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,da+\frac{1}{2\pi}\tilde{a}\,dg-\frac{2}{4\pi}g\,dg. (S56)

The gauge fields x=(a,γ,a~,g)x=(a,\gamma,\tilde{a},g) enter through 14​π​xT​K​d​x\frac{1}{4\pi}x^{T}K\,dx, with the integer matrix K=(4110)⊕(011−2)K=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}4&1\\ 1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\oplus\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\ 1&-2\end{smallmatrix}\bigr). Since detK=1\det K=1, all of these fields are gapped. The fermion ff couples through l=(1,1,1,0)l=(1,1,1,0), for which lT​K−1​l=0l^{T}K^{-1}l=0, and therefore retains no statistical interaction. The electromagnetic probe enters through tc=(1,0,0,0)t_{c}=(1,0,0,0), giving ff a charge −tcT​K−1​l=−1-t_{c}^{T}K^{-1}l=-1. Moreover, tcT​K−1​tc=0t_{c}^{T}K^{-1}t_{c}=0, so integrating out xx leaves no Hall response and yields

ℒ=ℒf​[−Ac],\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{f}[-A_{c}], (S57)

Therefore the trion Fermi liquid has no Hall conductance, since it cancels the response of the parent FCI in the same way as the Hall crystal (Sec. S4.6). The fermion ff carries the physical charge −1-1 of three anyons and couples to no dynamical gauge field, identifying it as a trion with finite overlap with the physical electron.

S4.4 Color states

Partons.

In the CB gauge we write the boson of flavor bb as ϕb=∑a=1Ncχa​ψa​b\phi_{b}=\sum_{a=1}^{N_{c}}\chi_{a}\psi_{ab}. The decomposition is invariant under χ→U​χ\chi\to U\chi, ψ→U∗​ψ\psi\to U^{*}\psi with U∈U\in U(NcN_{c}), so color is a gauge label and the parton gauge field β\beta is a U(NcN_{c}) field: χ\chi couples to a+βa+\beta and ψ\psi to −βT-\beta^{T}. Since U(NcN_{c})=[SU⁡(Nc)×U⁡(1)]/ℤNc=[\mathrm{SU}(N_{c})\times\mathrm{U}(1)]/\mathbb{Z}_{N_{c}}, β\beta cannot be split into independent SU(NcN_{c}) and U(1) fields with integer fluxes; its trace Tr​β\mathrm{Tr}\,\beta is an ordinary U(1) field, and we write its U(1) part as βc=1Nc​Tr​β\beta_{c}=\frac{1}{N_{c}}\mathrm{Tr}\,\beta. With the flux attachment of Eq. (S51), the parton theory reads

ℒ=ℒχ​[a+β]+ℒψ​[−βT]+Nc4​π​a​d​a+12​π​Ac​d​a,\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\chi}[a+\beta]+\mathcal{L}_{\psi}[-\beta^{T}]+\frac{N_{c}}{4\pi}a\,da+\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,da, (S58)

where ℒχ\mathcal{L}_{\chi} and ℒψ\mathcal{L}_{\psi} are the nonrelativistic Lagrangians of the partons minimally coupled to the indicated fields, and ℒψ\mathcal{L}_{\psi} also contains the holon interactions. Each color of χ\chi has density α​n\alpha n in the field b¯=−2​π​α​n\bar{b}=-2\pi\alpha n, giving a signed filling νχ=−1\nu_{\chi}=-1. Each color thus fills one reversed LL with Chern number −1-1. Integrating out the χ\chi fermions gives the U(NcN_{c})-1 term

−14​π​Tr​[(a+β)​d​(a+β)−2​i3​(a+β)3]=−Nc4​π​a​d​a−Nc2​π​a​d​βc−14​π​Tr​[β​d​β−2​i3​β3].-\frac{1}{4\pi}\mathrm{Tr}\Big[(a+\beta)d(a+\beta)-\tfrac{2\mathrm{i}}{3}(a+\beta)^{3}\Big]=-\frac{N_{c}}{4\pi}a\,da-\frac{N_{c}}{2\pi}a\,d\beta_{c}-\frac{1}{4\pi}\mathrm{Tr}\Big[\beta\,d\beta-\tfrac{2\mathrm{i}}{3}\beta^{3}\Big]. (S59)

Since m=1/α=Ncm=1/\alpha=N_{c}, the a​d​aa\,da terms cancel exactly, and the full theory becomes

ℒ=tr​ψ†​(i​Dt+𝐃22​mψ)​ψ+ℒint​[ψ]−14​π​Tr​(β​d​β−2​i3​β3)+12​π​a​d​(Ac−Nc​βc),\mathcal{L}=\mathrm{tr}\,\psi^{\dagger}\Big(\mathrm{i}D_{t}+\frac{\mathbf{D}^{2}}{2m_{\psi}}\Big)\psi+\mathcal{L}_{\rm int}[\psi]-\frac{1}{4\pi}\mathrm{Tr}\Big(\beta\,d\beta-\frac{2\mathrm{i}}{3}\beta^{3}\Big)+\frac{1}{2\pi}a\,d(A_{c}-N_{c}\beta_{c}), (S60)

with Dμψ=(∂μ+iβμT)ψD_{\mu}\psi=(\partial_{\mu}+\mathrm{i}\beta^{T}_{\mu})\psi, which is Eq. (6) for Nc=3N_{c}=3. The field aa enters only through the last term, so it acts as a Lagrange multiplier imposing βc=Ac/Nc\beta_{c}=A_{c}/N_{c}. Locally, we can write β=β^+βc​𝟙=β^+𝟙ℕ𝕔​𝔸𝕔​𝟙\beta=\hat{\beta}+\beta_{c}\openone=\hat{\beta}+\frac{1}{N_{c}}A_{c}\openone with traceless β^\hat{\beta}. The holons are then fermions of charge −1/Nc-1/N_{c} in zero net field, while the U(NcN_{c}) term separates into the FCI response −14​π​Nc​Ac​d​Ac-\frac{1}{4\pi N_{c}}A_{c}\,dA_{c} and an SU(NcN_{c})-1 gauge theory for β^\hat{\beta}. Globally, each flux quantum of AcA_{c} is accompanied by a ℤNc\mathbb{Z}_{N_{c}} flux of β^\hat{\beta}, ensuring consistency with the fractional holon charge. The auxiliary fermions χa\chi_{a} thus encode the U(NcN_{c})-1 term in a first-quantized anyon wavefunction. For Nc=3N_{c}=3, Eq. (6) reproduces the parton theory of the doped FCI in Ref. [41] with the opposite chirality.

Projection.

The physical wavefunction is obtained as the boson amplitude in the parton state, ΦB=⟨0|∏iϕbi​(𝐫i)​|Φχ⟩|Φψ⟩\Phi_{B}=\langle 0|\prod_{i}\phi_{b_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})|\Phi_{\chi}\rangle|\Phi_{\psi}\rangle, with the expansion of each ϕb\phi_{b} generating one term per coloring a=(a1,…,aN)a=(a_{1},\dots,a_{N}). Because each color level contains exactly k=N/Nck=N/N_{c} fermions, only colorings satisfying |Sc​(a)|=k|S_{c}(a)|=k contribute. Their χ\chi factor is sgn⁡(a)​∏cV¯Sc​(a)\mathrm{sgn}(a)\prod_{c}\bar{V}_{S_{c}(a)}, where sgn⁡(a)\mathrm{sgn}(a) is the sign of the permutation that sorts the particles by color; this sign is essential for Bose symmetry and gives Eq. (2). In the CB gauge each anyon experiences −α⁡(N−1)-\alpha(N-1) statistical flux quanta and has k−1k-1 antivortices in ∏cV¯Sc\prod_{c}\bar{V}_{S_{c}}, one on every other anyon of the same color, leaving zero effective field for the holons in the thermodynamic limit. Since every antivortex is bound to an anyon, these states contain no free vortices and describe liquids.

Descendants of the holon metal.

The phases derived from Eq. (6) are discussed in Ref. [41], and Table S1 summarizes those considered here. In the parent SU(3) holon metal, each of the nine species ψa​b\psi_{ab} fills a Fermi sea of density n/9n/9. Color-flavor-locked pairing produces the color superconductor, Φψ=Pf⁡[σi​j​g​(ξi,ξj)]\Phi_{\psi}=\mathrm{Pf}[\sigma_{ij}g(\xi_{i},\xi_{j})] with σi​j=∑AϵA​ai​aj​ϵA​bi​bj\sigma_{ij}=\sum_{A}\epsilon_{Aa_{i}a_{j}}\epsilon_{Ab_{i}b_{j}}, by locking color rotations to flavor rotations, SU(3)c×{}_{c}\timesSU(3)f→{}_{f}\toSU(3)diag [46, 47]. This completely Higgses the gauge field, while the gauge-invariant order parameter, a color singlet of three pairs, binds six anyons with charge 6​q=−26q=-2.

Low-energy theory of the color superconductor.

The color-flavor-locked condensate Higgses the SU(3) part of β\beta, so at low energies β=βc​𝟙\beta=\beta_{c}\openone with integer fluxes of βc\beta_{c}; a fractional flux of βc\beta_{c} requires a ℤ3\mathbb{Z}_{3} flux of the SU(3) part and binds a vortex of the condensate. A holon pair has charge −2-2 under βc\beta_{c}, so the phase θ\theta of the condensate enters through ρs2​(∂μθ+2​βc,μ)2\frac{\rho_{s}}{2}(\partial_{\mu}\theta+2\beta_{c,\mu})^{2}. We dualize it with a U(1) field bb whose flux measures the pair current, 12​π​ϵμ​ν​λ​∂νbλ=ρs​(∂μθ+2​βcμ)\frac{1}{2\pi}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\lambda}\partial_{\nu}b_{\lambda}=\rho_{s}(\partial^{\mu}\theta+2\beta_{c}^{\mu}), which replaces the condensate by −22​π​b​d​βc-\frac{2}{2\pi}b\,d\beta_{c} and a Maxwell term for bb. Setting β=βc​𝟙\beta=\beta_{c}\openone in Eq. (6) and adding this term gives

ℒSC=−34​π​βc​d​βc−32​π​a​d​βc−22​π​b​d​βc+12​π​Ac​d​a+⋯,\mathcal{L}_{\rm SC}=-\frac{3}{4\pi}\beta_{c}\,d\beta_{c}-\frac{3}{2\pi}a\,d\beta_{c}-\frac{2}{2\pi}b\,d\beta_{c}+\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,da+\cdots, (S61)

where the ellipsis denotes Maxwell terms. The self Chern–Simons term of βc\beta_{c} is the Hall response of the three filled χ\chi levels, which couple to a+βa+\beta. With β=βc​𝟙\beta=\beta_{c}\openone they give −34​π​(a+βc)​d​(a+βc)-\frac{3}{4\pi}(a+\beta_{c})d(a+\beta_{c}), whose a​d​aa\,da part cancels the flux attachment and leaves the first two terms of Eq. (S61). The gauge fields x=(a,βc,b)x=(a,\beta_{c},b) enter through 14​π​xT​K​d​x\frac{1}{4\pi}x^{T}K\,dx with K=(0−30−3−3−20−20)K=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-3&0\\ -3&-3&-2\\ 0&-2&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr), which has rank two. Its null vector x0=(2,0,−3)x_{0}=(2,0,-3) carries only a Maxwell term, so this combination is a gapless photon, dual to the phase of a superfluid. The probe enters through tc=(1,0,0)t_{c}=(1,0,0), and tc⋅x0=2t_{c}\cdot x_{0}=2 is the charge of the condensed boson, three holon pairs or six anyons.

To find the remaining quasiparticles, note that an excitation carries an integer charge vector l∈ℤ3l\in\mathbb{Z}^{3}, one integer for each of the three U(1) fields in xx, since each field has 2​π2\pi-quantized fluxes. Its charge under the gapless photon is l⋅x0l\cdot x_{0}. An excitation with l⋅x0≠0l\cdot x_{0}\neq 0 is a vortex of the superfluid, whose energy grows logarithmically with the system size, so finite-energy excitations have l⋅x0=0l\cdot x_{0}=0. Among them are the charges that the Chern–Simons terms bind to 2​π​n2\pi n of flux of the internal fields xx (not of the probe AcA_{c}), l=K​nl=Kn for an integer vector nn. For example, a 2​π2\pi flux of bb, which adds one pair, binds a holon pair, l=(0,−2,0)l=(0,-2,0), and a 2​π2\pi flux of aa binds three holons, l=(0,−3,0)l=(0,-3,0), with the charge of an electron of the parent FCI. Since K​x0=0Kx_{0}=0, these objects have l⋅x0=0l\cdot x_{0}=0 and are not vortices. They are created by monopole events of the compact fields xx, and their Aharonov–Bohm phase with any excitation l′l^{\prime} is 2​π​n⋅l′2\pi n\cdot l^{\prime}, so they are local. The distinct anyon types are therefore the finite-energy charges modulo K​ℤ3K\mathbb{Z}^{3}. To count them we use the Smith normal form: any integer matrix can be written as K=U​D​VK=UDV, with UU and VV integer matrices of determinant ±1\pm 1 and D=diag⁡(d1,d2,d3)D=\mathrm{diag}(d_{1},d_{2},d_{3}), so that ℤ3/K​ℤ3≅⨁iℤ/di​ℤ\mathbb{Z}^{3}/K\mathbb{Z}^{3}\cong\bigoplus_{i}\mathbb{Z}/d_{i}\mathbb{Z}. A zero entry gives a free factor ℤ\mathbb{Z}, measured by l⋅x0l\cdot x_{0}, which counts vortices. The anyons are the finite factors: an entry di>1d_{i}>1 would give ℤdi\mathbb{Z}_{d_{i}} anyons and a factor did_{i} in the torus degeneracy. Here D=diag⁡(1,1,0)D=\mathrm{diag}(1,1,0), so the gapped sector has no anyons.

On the other hand, adjoint Higgs fields that lock the color and flavor indices instead reduce the gauge group to U(1)2 or Z3: the former gives the U(1)2 metal and its inter-flavor paired superconductor, while the latter gives the Type I triplet Z3Z_{3} metal and the singlet Z3 metals.

The U(1)2 metal and its paired descendant.

A particle–hole Higgs field can select the three diagonal holons fb=ψb​bf_{b}=\psi_{bb} and raise the energies of the six off-diagonal species. The remaining gauge transformations are diagonal color rotations with unit determinant. There are two independent phases, giving U(1)2. Writing the surviving traceless gauge field as β^=diag⁡(b1,b2,b3)\hat{\beta}=\mathrm{diag}(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}), Eq. (6) reduces locally to

ℒU​(1)2=∑b=13ℒfb​[−bb−Ac/3]−14​π​∑b=13bb​d​bb−112​π​Ac​d​Ac,∑bbb=0.\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{U}(1)^{2}}=\sum_{b=1}^{3}\mathcal{L}_{f_{b}}[-b_{b}-A_{c}/3]-\frac{1}{4\pi}\sum_{b=1}^{3}b_{b}\,db_{b}-\frac{1}{12\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c},\qquad\sum_{b}b_{b}=0. (S62)

We have three Fermi seas of holons with charge −e/3-e/3, each of density n/3n/3, couple to two continuous gauge fields [26, 37, 41]. The diagonal selection chooses a flavor basis and intrinsically breaks the SU(3) flavor symmetry down to S3S_{3}.

The mean-field holon wavefunction is a product of three flavor determinants. Only ai=bia_{i}=b_{i} contributes to the color projection, giving Eq. (S23), or its CF form in Eq. (S24). The U(1)2 superconductor replaces these determinants by an inter-flavor pp-wave Pfaffian.

The singlet and Type I triplet Z3 metals.

Higgs fields that lock all color generators to flavor generators leave only the center of SU(3) as a gauge symmetry. Unlike the U(1)2 metal, these states preserve a global SU(3), realized by a flavor rotation combined with a compensating color rotation [41]. To specify the two locks in our conventions, let UU act on color and VV on the physical flavor, so that ψ→U∗​ψ​VT\psi\to U^{*}\psi V^{T}. The ordinary lock U=VU=V selects ψ0=tr​ψ/3\psi_{0}=\mathrm{tr}\,\psi/\sqrt{3} and gaps the orthogonal octet. This flavor singlet fills one Fermi sea of density nn. Since its amplitude is proportional to δa​b\delta_{ab}, the projected ansatz again has only ai=bia_{i}=b_{i}. It contains three filled lowest-LL factors and a single holon determinant over all NN particles, as in Sec. S1.3.

The conjugate lock U=V∗U=V^{*} instead selects the antisymmetric subspace, ηA=∑a​bϵA​a​b​ψa​b/2\eta_{A}=\sum_{ab}\epsilon_{Aab}\psi_{ab}/\sqrt{2}, and gaps the symmetric sextet. Filling one Fermi sea of density n/3n/3 for each AA gives the Type I triplet Z3 metal. For a fixed coloring, its holon Slater matrix has entries ϵA​ai​bi​Vm​(i)/2\epsilon_{Aa_{i}b_{i}}V_{m}(i)/\sqrt{2}, with N/3N/3 occupied orbitals mm per pocket AA. An anyon of flavor bb can therefore carry either color a≠ba\neq b. The projection retains a sum over colorings, rather than a single product. With k=N/3k=N/3 particles of each flavor, the number of allowed balanced colorings is ∑x=0k(kx)3\sum_{x=0}^{k}\binom{k}{x}^{3}. A fixed permutation of color and flavor only relabels the colors and cannot reproduce this antisymmetric projection.

In both Z3 descendants, the continuous color gauge fluctuations are massive, while a discrete gauge field remains. The low-energy matter consists of one or three Fermi pockets of holons with charge −e/3-e/3 and nontrivial Z3 gauge charge. The discrete gauge sector inherits its topological term from SU(3)-1 in Eq. (6). These are fractionalized metals: a gapless holon is not a local electron, and the Fermi surface need not give an electron quasiparticle pole.

The Type II triplet Z3 metal.

The construction of Ref. [39] instead writes ϕb=d​Ψb\phi_{b}=d\,\Psi_{b}, with a flavor-singlet fermion dd and a flavor-triplet fermion Ψb\Psi_{b}. The parton dd fills three reversed LLs, with total Chern number −3-3, while each Ψb\Psi_{b} forms a Fermi sea of density n/3n/3 in zero mean field. The corresponding CB wavefunction is

ΦBII=χ¯3​∏b=13deti∈b[Vm​(i)].\Phi_{B}^{\rm II}=\bar{\chi}_{3}\prod_{b=1}^{3}\det_{i\in b}[V_{m}(i)]. (S63)

Here χ¯3\bar{\chi}_{3} is one determinant of three filled reversed LLs over all particles. There is no color sum. Let γ\gamma be the parton U(1) gauge field, with dd coupled to a+γa+\gamma and Ψb\Psi_{b} to −γ-\gamma. Integrating out dd adds −3(a+γ)d(a+γ)/(4π)-3(a+\gamma)d(a+\gamma)/(4\pi) to Eq. (S51). The a​d​aa\,da terms cancel, leaving

ℒII=∑bℒΨb​[−γ]−34​π​γ​d​γ+12​π​a​d​(Ac−3​γ).\mathcal{L}_{\rm II}=\sum_{b}\mathcal{L}_{\Psi_{b}}[-\gamma]-\frac{3}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma+\frac{1}{2\pi}a\,d(A_{c}-3\gamma). (S64)

The compact field aa imposes 3​γ=Ac3\gamma=A_{c} locally, so the fermions have charge −e/3-e/3. Globally, the factor of three leaves a Z3 gauge field; the γ​d​γ\gamma\,d\gamma term specifies its twist. We omit gravitational response terms here.

Both triplet constructions therefore have three fractional-charge Fermi pockets and discrete gauge structure, but their parton content and flavor action differ. In Type I, the three filled lowest LLs carry color, and conjugate locking acts as ψ→V​ψ​VT\psi\to V\psi V^{T}, giving η→V∗​η\eta\to V^{*}\eta. In Type II, the filled parton is a flavor singlet and the gapless fermions transform as Ψ→V​Ψ\Psi\to V\Psi. Taking the physical anyon to be an SU(3) fundamental, the three Fermi pockets therefore form an antifundamental multiplet in Type I and a fundamental multiplet in Type II.

Sphere flux and closed shells.

On the sphere, a metallic mean-field state is rotation invariant only if every Fermi pocket fills complete angular-momentum shells. This fixes which sizes NN and sectors qb​gq_{bg} we can use for each metal. By Eq. (S42), the holons of the color construction see the flux 2​Qψ=qb​g−2/32Q_{\psi}=q_{bg}-2/3, and their shells have angular momentum l=|Qψ|,|Qψ|+1,…l=|Q_{\psi}|,|Q_{\psi}|+1,\ldots with 2​l+12l+1 orbitals each. At qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 or 5/35/3, where |2​Qψ|=1|2Q_{\psi}|=1, the shells hold 2,4,6,…2,4,6,\ldots holons, so a pocket is closed with 2,6,12,…2,6,12,\ldots holons. At qb​g=2/3q_{bg}=2/3, where 2​Qψ=02Q_{\psi}=0, the shells hold 1,3,5,…1,3,5,\ldots holons, and a pocket is closed with 1,4,9,…1,4,9,\ldots holons. The total NN is this occupation times the number of pockets: nine for the SU(3) holon metal, three for the U(1)2 and Type I triplet Z3 metals, and one for the singlet Z3 metal. At qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3, for example, the holon metal is closed at N=18N=18 and the three-pocket metals at N=6N=6 and 18.

The Type II triplet Z3 metal sits in a different sector because its filled parton differs. The parton dd fills three reversed LLs, which requires the flux 2​Qd=3−N/32Q_{d}=3-N/3. Subtracting this from the CB flux 2​QB=qb​g−(N−1)/32Q_{B}=q_{bg}-(N-1)/3 of Sec. S1.1 leaves 2​QΨ=qb​g−8/32Q_{\Psi}=q_{bg}-8/3 for the fermions Ψb\Psi_{b}. Zero-flux Fermi seas of Ψb\Psi_{b} therefore require qb​g=8/3q_{bg}=8/3, where the three pockets are closed at N=12,27,…N=12,27,\ldots (three filled LLs of dd need N≥9N\geq 9). This shift comes from the different filled-LL factor and does not by itself distinguish the metallic phases. The paired color states need no closed shells. A J=0J=0 pair in the p∓i​pp\mp ip channel, however, requires 2​Qψ=∓12Q_{\psi}=\mp 1, that is, qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 or 5/35/3.

Chirality and chiral central charge.

We adopt the orientation appropriate to tMoTe2 (Sec. S4.6), for which the parent FCI in Eq. (S51) has σx​y=−13e2/h\sigma_{xy}=-\frac{1}{3}\,e^{2}/h, as does the doped FCI component of the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 state. Equation (6) therefore has the opposite chirality to the theory in Ref. [41], whose FCI has σx​y=+13e2/h\sigma_{xy}=+\frac{1}{3}\,e^{2}/h.

We label a paired state by the winding ℓ\ell of ⟨ψ𝐤​ψ−𝐤⟩∝ei​ℓ​ϑ𝐤\langle\psi_{\mathbf{k}}\psi_{-\mathbf{k}}\rangle\propto\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\ell\vartheta_{\mathbf{k}}}, the eigenvalue of Lz=−i∂ϑL_{z}=-\mathrm{i}\partial_{\vartheta}. A weakly paired pocket has BdG Chern number −ℓ-\ell and contributes c−=−ℓ/2c_{-}=-\ell/2 [41], in the orientation in which a filled LL in a positive field contributes +1+1. A J=0J=0 pair in holon flux 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} has ℓ=2​Qψ\ell=2Q_{\psi}, so the color superconductor is p−i​pp-ip (ℓ=−1\ell=-1) at qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 and p+i​pp+ip at qb​g=5/3q_{bg}=5/3. The Chern–Simons term selects ℓ=−1\ell=-1 in our orientation [41], the sector in which the color superconductor lies furthest below the crystal (Sec. S5.3). With SU(3) gauge field Higgsed completely, the three χ\chi levels contribute 3×(−1)3\times(-1) and the nine holon pockets 9×129\times\frac{1}{2}: the doped FCI contributes c−=32c_{-}=\frac{3}{2}. Together with the filled C=1C=1 band of the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 state, we have c−=52c_{-}=\frac{5}{2} in total. Three anyons make one carrier of the parent FCI, c∼ψ†​ψ†​ψ†c\sim\psi^{\dagger}\psi^{\dagger}\psi^{\dagger} up to the filled χ\chi levels, so the charge-2​e2e pairs have angular momentum L=−3​ℓ=3L=-3\ell=3: they are in f+i​ff+if channel[41]. A BCS superconductor of the same carriers with the same L=3L=3 has one pocket with c−=−32c_{-}=-\frac{3}{2}, and together with the ν=1\nu=1 background, we have c−=1−32=−12c_{-}=1-\frac{3}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}. The two superconductors have the same pairing symmetry, but their c−c_{-} differ by 3.

Semions with Nc=2N_{c}=2: the color superconductor.

For Nc=2N_{c}=2 the same construction, with βc=Ac/2\beta_{c}=A_{c}/2, leaves color doublets of charge −1/2-1/2 coupled to SU(2)-1, at holon flux 2​Qψ=qb​g−122Q_{\psi}=q_{bg}-\frac{1}{2}. A J=0J=0 pair in flux 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} has relative angular momentum 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} in the planar coordinate zz (holomorphic for 2​Qψ>02Q_{\psi}>0), so the closed-shell sectors qb​g=−3/2q_{bg}=-3/2 (spinless) and −1/2-1/2 [SU(2)] give d−i​dd-id and p−i​pp-ip pairs (ℓ=−2\ell=-2 and −1-1 in the notation above). Color-singlet pairing, Φψ=Pf⁡[ϵai​aj​gi​j]\Phi_{\psi}=\mathrm{Pf}[\epsilon_{a_{i}a_{j}}g_{ij}] (spinless, d−i​dd-id) or Pf⁡[ϵai​aj​ϵfi​fj​gi​j]\mathrm{Pf}[\epsilon_{a_{i}a_{j}}\epsilon_{f_{i}f_{j}}g_{ij}] [SU(2), spin-singlet p−i​pp-ip], gives a condensate of charge −1-1, a pair of semions, which leads to the same paired superfluid phase as in the CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 description. The final phase has chiral central charge c−=0c_{-}=0: the two χ\chi levels contribute 2×(−1)2\times(-1), the paired holon pockets 2×12\times 1 (spinless, ℓ=−2\ell=-2) or 4×124\times\frac{1}{2} [SU(2), ℓ=−1\ell=-1], and the color SU(2) gauge field, whose level −1-1 CS term is canceled by the pairing of the holons, confines and adds nothing. In the context of doping a bosonic Laughlin state (or a chiral spin liquid), the final phase is an ordinary superfluid of the physical bosons, without topological order. For SU(2) semions the spin sector stays chiral, with the spin Hall response of Sec. S4.2, and the charge sector compensates to reach c−=0c_{-}=0.

S4.5 Hyperdeterminant structure and color channels

The color projection gives a direct connection between the SU(3) holon metal and hyperdeterminant wavefunctions [76, 77, 78]. We first consider the unpaired mean-field state and omit the common statistical phase, contact factor and Jastrow factor. The parton decomposition is

ϕb​(𝐫)=∑a=13χa​(𝐫)​ψa​b​(𝐫),\phi_{b}(\mathbf{r})=\sum_{a=1}^{3}\chi_{a}(\mathbf{r})\psi_{ab}(\mathbf{r}), (S65)

where χ\chi and ψ\psi are fermions, aa is the gauge color and bb is the physical flavor. For NN composite bosons, each fermionic parton sector contains NN particles. Let χμ​a​(𝐫)\chi_{\mu a}(\mathbf{r}) and uν,a​b​(𝐫)u_{\nu,ab}(\mathbf{r}) be its occupied one-particle orbitals, with μ,ν=1,…,N\mu,\nu=1,\ldots,N. These labels run over the chosen occupied subspaces, including their color and flavor indices. For the SU(3) holon metal, a basis with definite color and flavor has μ=(c,m)\mu=(c,m) and ν=(d,s,ℓ)\nu=(d,s,\ell). Here c,dc,d label color, ss labels flavor, and m,ℓm,\ell label the spatial orbitals of χ\chi and ψ\psi, respectively. The local field components ai,bia_{i},b_{i} are matched to these occupied-state labels through

χ(c,m),ai​(𝐫i)=δc​ai​φm​(𝐫i),u(d,s,ℓ),ai​bi​(𝐫i)=δd​ai​δs​bi​vℓ​(𝐫i).\chi_{(c,m),a_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})=\delta_{ca_{i}}\varphi_{m}(\mathbf{r}_{i}),\qquad u_{(d,s,\ell),a_{i}b_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})=\delta_{da_{i}}\delta_{sb_{i}}v_{\ell}(\mathbf{r}_{i}). (S66)

Thus the occupied χ\chi and holon orbitals must have the same color c=d=aic=d=a_{i}, and the holon flavor must equal the physical flavor s=bis=b_{i}. The color aia_{i} is summed over, while bib_{i} is fixed by the sampled configuration xi=(𝐫i,bi)x_{i}=(\mathbf{r}_{i},b_{i}). Projection gives, up to an overall normalization and a configuration-independent sign,

ΦB(0)​(x1,…,xN)=∑a1,…,aNdeti​μ[χμ​ai​(𝐫i)]​deti​ν[uν,ai​bi​(𝐫i)].\Phi_{B}^{(0)}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{N})=\sum_{a_{1},\ldots,a_{N}}\det_{i\mu}[\chi_{\mu a_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})]\,\det_{i\nu}[u_{\nu,a_{i}b_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})]. (S67)

The color-permutation sign in Eq. (2) is already present in the full χ\chi determinant here. Only colorings with N/3N/3 particles of each color contribute. For these colorings, order the columns by color and sort the rows into the sets Sc​(a)={i:ai=c}S_{c}(a)=\{i:a_{i}=c\}. This gives

deti​μ[χμ​ai​(𝐫i)]=sgn⁡(a)​∏c=13deti∈Sc​(a),m[φm​(𝐫i)].\det_{i\mu}[\chi_{\mu a_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})]=\operatorname{sgn}(a)\prod_{c=1}^{3}\det_{i\in S_{c}(a),m}[\varphi_{m}(\mathbf{r}_{i})]. (S68)

Rows within each set retain their original particle order. This is the explicit sign used when writing the χ\chi wavefunction as a product of color determinants in Eq. (2). In Eq. (S67), it remains inside the unsplit determinant, so inserting another sgn⁡(a)\operatorname{sgn}(a) would count it twice. If both parton determinants are split into color blocks, their two row-sorting signs cancel.

Expand the two determinants as sums over permutations σ,τ\sigma,\tau of their occupied columns. For fixed σ,τ\sigma,\tau, the color aia_{i} appears only in the local product χσ⁡(i),ai​(𝐫i)​uτ⁡(i),ai​bi​(𝐫i)\chi_{\sigma(i),a_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})u_{\tau(i),a_{i}b_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i}). The sum over all a1,…,aNa_{1},\ldots,a_{N} therefore factorizes into a product of NN local color sums, one for each particle. Defining the fusion tensor

Ti;μ​ν=∑a=13χμ​a​(𝐫i)​uν,a​bi​(𝐫i),T_{i;\mu\nu}=\sum_{a=1}^{3}\chi_{\mu a}(\mathbf{r}_{i})u_{\nu,ab_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i}), (S69)

we obtain

ΦB(0)=HdetB⁡(T)≡∑σ,τ∈SNsgn⁡(σ)​sgn⁡(τ)​∏i=1NTi;σ⁡(i)​τ​(i).\Phi_{B}^{(0)}=\operatorname{Hdet}_{B}(T)\equiv\sum_{\sigma,\tau\in S_{N}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\prod_{i=1}^{N}T_{i;\sigma(i)\tau(i)}. (S70)

This is the bosonic combinatorial hyperdeterminant: the two occupied-orbital indices are antisymmetrized, while exchanging two physical particles produces two canceling signs. The tensor has size N×N×NN\times N\times N for each sampled configuration. Its entries are built from parton orbitals.

One channel versus three channels.

For a fixed physical coordinate and flavor xix_{i}, regard the fusion tensor as an N×NN\times N matrix. Its rows label occupied χ\chi orbitals and its columns label occupied holon orbitals:

Ti≡(Ti;11Ti;12⋯Ti;1​NTi;21Ti;22⋯Ti;2​N⋱Ti;N​1Ti;N​2⋯Ti;N​N)=∑a=13𝝌a​(𝐫i)​[𝐮a​bi​(𝐫i)]T.T_{i}\equiv\begin{pmatrix}T_{i;11}&T_{i;12}&\cdots&T_{i;1N}\\ T_{i;21}&T_{i;22}&\cdots&T_{i;2N}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\ T_{i;N1}&T_{i;N2}&\cdots&T_{i;NN}\end{pmatrix}=\sum_{a=1}^{3}\bm{\chi}_{a}(\mathbf{r}_{i})\bigl[\mathbf{u}_{ab_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})\bigr]^{T}. (S71)

The NN-component column vectors use the same orbital amplitudes as Eq. (S69): [𝝌a​(𝐫i)]μ=χμ​a​(𝐫i)[\bm{\chi}_{a}(\mathbf{r}_{i})]_{\mu}=\chi_{\mu a}(\mathbf{r}_{i}) and [𝐮a​bi​(𝐫i)]ν=uν,a​bi​(𝐫i)[\mathbf{u}_{ab_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})]_{\nu}=u_{\nu,ab_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i}). A channel is one outer product of these vectors, labeled here by color aa. The minimum number of outer products required is the matrix rank of TiT_{i}; we use RR for its generic value. Equivalently, in orthonormal bases of the two occupied subspaces, TiT_{i} defines a normalized two-parton amplitude

|Ti⟩=1‖Ti‖F​∑μ,ν=1NTi;μ​ν​|μ⟩χ⊗|ν⟩ψ,‖Ti‖F2=∑μ,ν|Ti;μ​ν|2.|T_{i}\rangle=\frac{1}{\|T_{i}\|_{F}}\sum_{\mu,\nu=1}^{N}T_{i;\mu\nu}\,|\mu\rangle_{\chi}\otimes|\nu\rangle_{\psi},\qquad\|T_{i}\|_{F}^{2}=\sum_{\mu,\nu}|T_{i;\mu\nu}|^{2}. (S72)

Its Schmidt rank is RR. Thus R=1R=1 gives independent, separable χ\chi and holon amplitudes, whereas R>1R>1 entangles their orbital indices. This entanglement resides in the local fusion map used to project the two mean-field Slater determinants. A conventional product construction has R=1R=1, namely Ti;μ​ν=Ti;μχ​Ti;νψT_{i;\mu\nu}=T^{\chi}_{i;\mu}T^{\psi}_{i;\nu}. Equation (S70) then factorizes exactly into det[Ti;μχ]​det[Ti;νψ]\det[T^{\chi}_{i;\mu}]\det[T^{\psi}_{i;\nu}]. This includes both the singlet Z3 metal, with effective decomposition ϕb=χb​f\phi_{b}=\chi_{b}f, and the Type II triplet Z3 metal, ϕb=d​Ψb\phi_{b}=d\,\Psi_{b} of Eq. (S63).

In Eq. (S69), the channel is instead the contracted color aa. The SU(3) holon metal has R=3R=3: its three color contributions are independent, as the example below makes explicit. Color is summed over and is not assigned to a physical particle in advance. The occupied orbitals include complete color triplets, and the determinants enforce the occupation of every selected orbital once. Thus the projection sums all compatible color assignments.

A simple illustration with nine particles.

Consider N=9N=9 anyons, with three particles of each physical flavor. Let the reversed mean field contain Nϕ=3N_{\phi}=3 flux quanta for χa\chi_{a}, so its lowest LL has three orbitals φm\varphi_{m}, m=1,2,3m=1,2,3. In the zero-field holon ψa​b\psi_{ab} sector, we only consider the 𝐤=0\mathbf{k}=0 orbital v0(𝐫)=𝒮−1/2v_{0}(\mathbf{r})=\mathcal{S}^{-1/2}, where 𝒮\mathcal{S} is the system area. The SU(3) color state occupies all nine χ\chi orbitals (a,m)(a,m) and all nine holon orbitals (c,d,𝐤=0)(c,d,\mathbf{k}=0), where a,ca,c are colors and dd is flavor. To display the bases, write |a,m⟩χ=|a⟩color⊗|φm⟩|a,m\rangle_{\chi}=|a\rangle_{\rm color}\otimes|\varphi_{m}\rangle and |c,d⟩ψ=|c⟩color⊗|d⟩flavor⊗|𝐤=0⟩|c,d\rangle_{\psi}=|c\rangle_{\rm color}\otimes|d\rangle_{\rm flavor}\otimes|\mathbf{k}=0\rangle. The two occupied bases are

ℬχ=(|1,1⟩χ|1,2⟩χ|1,3⟩χ|2,1⟩χ|2,2⟩χ|2,3⟩χ|3,1⟩χ|3,2⟩χ|3,3⟩χ),ℬψ=(|1,1⟩ψ|1,2⟩ψ|1,3⟩ψ|2,1⟩ψ|2,2⟩ψ|2,3⟩ψ|3,1⟩ψ|3,2⟩ψ|3,3⟩ψ).\mathcal{B}_{\chi}=\begin{pmatrix}|1,1\rangle_{\chi}&|1,2\rangle_{\chi}&|1,3\rangle_{\chi}\\ |2,1\rangle_{\chi}&|2,2\rangle_{\chi}&|2,3\rangle_{\chi}\\ |3,1\rangle_{\chi}&|3,2\rangle_{\chi}&|3,3\rangle_{\chi}\end{pmatrix},\qquad\mathcal{B}_{\psi}=\begin{pmatrix}|1,1\rangle_{\psi}&|1,2\rangle_{\psi}&|1,3\rangle_{\psi}\\ |2,1\rangle_{\psi}&|2,2\rangle_{\psi}&|2,3\rangle_{\psi}\\ |3,1\rangle_{\psi}&|3,2\rangle_{\psi}&|3,3\rangle_{\psi}\end{pmatrix}. (S73)

Each row has a fixed color. The columns of ℬχ\mathcal{B}_{\chi} distinguish LLL orbitals, while those of ℬψ\mathcal{B}_{\psi} distinguish flavors. Every entry in both arrays is occupied once, as illustrated in Fig. S4. We fix the ordering by reading each array row by row: μ=3​(a−1)+m\mu=3(a-1)+m and ν=3​(c−1)+d\nu=3(c-1)+d. The corresponding orbital amplitudes are χ(a,m),a′​(𝐫)=δa​a′​φm​(𝐫)\chi_{(a,m),a^{\prime}}(\mathbf{r})=\delta_{aa^{\prime}}\varphi_{m}(\mathbf{r}) and u(c,d),a′​b​(𝐫)=δc​a′​δd​b​v0​(𝐫)u_{(c,d),a^{\prime}b}(\mathbf{r})=\delta_{ca^{\prime}}\delta_{db}v_{0}(\mathbf{r}). Thus the 9×9×99\times 9\times 9 fusion tensor is

Ti;(a,m)​(c,d)=δa​c​φm​(𝐫i)​δd​bi​v0​(𝐫i),a,c,m,d=1,2,3.T_{i;(a,m)(c,d)}=\delta_{ac}\,\varphi_{m}(\mathbf{r}_{i})\delta_{db_{i}}\,v_{0}(\mathbf{r}_{i}),\qquad a,c,m,d=1,2,3. (S74)

For a fixed particle ii with physical flavor bi=1b_{i}=1, the matrix in these bases is explicitly

Ti=v0​(𝐫i)​(φ100000000φ200000000φ300000000000φ100000000φ200000000φ300000000000φ100000000φ200000000φ300),φm≡φm​(𝐫i).T_{i}=v_{0}(\mathbf{r}_{i})\left(\begin{array}[]{ccc|ccc|ccc}\varphi_{1}&0&0&0&0&0&0&0&0\\ \varphi_{2}&0&0&0&0&0&0&0&0\\ \varphi_{3}&0&0&0&0&0&0&0&0\\ \hline\cr 0&0&0&\varphi_{1}&0&0&0&0&0\\ 0&0&0&\varphi_{2}&0&0&0&0&0\\ 0&0&0&\varphi_{3}&0&0&0&0&0\\ \hline\cr 0&0&0&0&0&0&\varphi_{1}&0&0\\ 0&0&0&0&0&0&\varphi_{2}&0&0\\ 0&0&0&0&0&0&\varphi_{3}&0&0\end{array}\right),\qquad\varphi_{m}\equiv\varphi_{m}(\mathbf{r}_{i}). (S75)

The separators mark the three color sectors. Only columns ν=1,4,7\nu=1,4,7 are nonzero, since these are the flavor-1 holon orbitals of colors 1, 2 and 3. All particles use the same ordered lists of nine occupied χ\chi orbitals and nine occupied ψ\psi orbitals. The matrix TiT_{i} evaluates their amplitudes at particle ii’s position and physical flavor; changing ii does not change the occupied orbital basis. The full hyperdeterminant uses every occupied column once across the nine particles. Each diagonal 3×33\times 3 color block has rank one. The three blocks have disjoint row and column supports, giving rank⁡Ti=3\operatorname{rank}T_{i}=3. The normalized amplitude in Eq. (S72) therefore has three equal Schmidt coefficients 1/31/\sqrt{3}. The χ\chi and holon colors are entangled: their colors must match, and all three matches enter coherently. Neither parton has a fixed color of its own in this fusion amplitude. All nine χ\chi fermions fit in the LLL, with three per color, while all nine holons fit at 𝐤=0\mathbf{k}=0, with one per color and flavor. Projection combines one fermion from each parton sector into each composite boson.
